issues.quote: Monsieur Félix would not let anyone touch his late father's silver watch, and he would not let the master touch it either.
issues.fact: The fact sheet says nothing about which watch Félix owned, whether it was the silver heirloom, or whether the master ever adjusted it. L1 only gives Félix's watch as twenty minutes behind.
issues.misreading: A solver could read this as identifying the watch Félix showed at dinner as the untouched silver heirloom, so that its twenty-minute error is treated as his own and never corrected. That adds a link between the watch and its history that the sheet does not support.

issues.quote: When you press the slide, it sounds the time. Low notes for the hours, a doubled note for each quarter, and high notes for each minute past the quarter.
issues.fact: The fact sheet contains no repeater, and gives no time source other than the bell, the regulator, the watches and the kitchen and Rosa's clocks.
issues.misreading: A solver could treat the repeater as an independent, exact way to read the time at some moment, or as a clue to a particular time, which the sheet does not supply.

issues.quote: He taught me to count the beats in my head so I would not need to look at a watch.
issues.fact: The fact sheet gives no counting, beat-timing or duration information.
issues.misreading: A solver could read this as a hint that elapsed time was estimated by counting, implying an unstated duration or an unreliable interval between the readings.
